candidates.name: Estimate-path check for residential cleaning firms
candidates.buyer: Owner of an independent residential cleaning firm with an existing website and estimate-request route.
candidates.problem: A broken or unclear estimate path could waste acquisition effort; frequency and monetary impact are unverified.
candidates.offer: Fixed-scope evidence-backed issue report and webmaster tickets, not a website rebuild.
candidates.acquisition: Provisional Raleigh-only manual discovery: review at most 10 official residential-cleaning websites in at most two hours; verify segment, estimate route and whether a relevant business-contact channel exists. Record source URL/date and unknown ownership; do not compile personal contacts. Mason then approves a maximum five interview invitations and exact messages/channel separately. No invitations sent; discovered sites are not qualified leads.
candidates.delivery: Agree URL/scope; inspect allowed public route; collect screenshots/reproduction; review findings; deliver prioritized tickets; record acceptance and timing.
costDrivers: Any later approved inference; none now
assumptions: An actionable report is worth a provisional USD 149.
Mason can reach buyers and judge functional claims.
candidates.validation: Five bounded interviews and a sample review; seek a request for written pilot scope, not hypothetical praise.
candidates.why: Small deliverable and short learning loop reuse evidence, review and outcome controls without creating a new platform. Buyer access is the largest weakness.

candidates.name: Contact-path release QA for small web agencies
candidates.buyer: Owner or project manager of a small agency shipping service-business websites.
candidates.problem: Late contact-path defects can create client rework; our frequency and impact are unknown.
candidates.offer: White-label pre-launch functional check and reproducible release tickets.
candidates.acquisition: Owner-approved introductions or individually selected agency business contact channel; no relationship assumed.
candidates.delivery: Agency supplies permitted staging URL and release criteria; inspect and report; agency owns fixes and release.
assumptions: An unproven external reviewer is trusted.
candidates.validation: Interview agency owners about last release and existing QA; show the same sample and ask what would make it usable.
candidates.why: Could rank first if Mason already has agency access; currently stronger competition and unknown trust/access make it less immediately grounded.

candidates.name: Monthly review-theme action digest
candidates.buyer: Single-location service owner with enough owner-permitted reviews to reveal recurring issues.
candidates.problem: Feedback might not become operational action; frequency and willingness to pay are unknown.
candidates.offer: Source-linked themes, unresolved questions and proposed actions; no public replies or review solicitation.
candidates.acquisition: Owner-approved interviews with local operators; no owned audience assumed.
candidates.delivery: Receive permitted corpus; summarize with source links; owner reviews actions; track whether anything changes.
assumptions: Digest changes decisions rather than duplicating tools.
Owner has enough feedback and permission to use it.
candidates.validation: Ask owners to show their current process; request an action they would take from an example before offering recurrence.
candidates.why: Established substitutes and recurring attention burden are less attractive before any buyer is known.

sample.provenance: Illustrative invented company and deliberately seeded defects; development-assistant authored. No customer website was audited.

findings.issue: Estimate link has no matching fragment target
findings.evidence: Request an estimate; no id="estimate" exists
findings.fix: Point to the owner-confirmed contact section, then retest pointer/keyboard navigation.

findings.evidence: Hero says North County; contact says South County only.
findings.fix: Ask owner; do not choose or silently edit.

findings.evidence: Send details has no contact method or process.
findings.fix: Insert owner-approved contact method; do not invent a reply deadline.

interview: How did your last three estimate requests reach you? What is verifiable?
When did a customer last report a failed or confusing contact process? Record never if none.
Who checks after changes and who fixes defects? What effort does that require?
What makes an outside report unnecessary? What is more urgent?
Which sample finding would you act on or ignore, and why?
Would you request a written USD 149 pilot scope? Who decides? This is a price test, not a sale.
May we follow up? Record explicit permission separately.

outreach.subject: A question about how you check your estimate-request page
outreach.body: Hi [name], I'm Mason. I'm exploring a small service that checks the route from a service-business website to an estimate request and gives the owner a short, reproducible fix list. I have not audited your site and am not claiming you have a problem. Could I ask for 15 minutes about how you currently check that route and who handles fixes? I can show a clearly labeled sample. If this is not relevant, no need to reply. [Owner-approved identity/contact details]

discoveryProcedure: Choose Raleigh as a reversible research geography; Mason may substitute a place with better permitted access before recruiting.

Search public web for Raleigh residential cleaning estimate. Open official business websites manually; stop at 10 distinct firms or two hours, whichever comes first. Deduplicate franchises/brands and reject commercial-only sites.

Record only official domain, service geography, residential scope, visible estimate route, existence of a suitable business-contact channel, retrieval date and ownership unknowns. Do not scrape personal details or infer an owner email.
Rank by segment fit and ability to act on a report, not alleged defects or flattering predictions. Sites with good existing processes may be unsuitable; retain that negative evidence.
Present up to five possible invitations with exact recipient/channel/message for separate owner approval; these must not be sent through customer quote forms disguised as cleaning inquiries.
After approved invitations, cap completed discovery interviews at five. No automatic extra invitations or repeated follow-up; any shortfall is missing evidence, not permission to expand the bound.
If no suitable channel or owner access emerges, stop this recruitment route. Prefer an actual introduction/agency access if Mason supplies one; otherwise reassess the venture before new tooling.
